# Using elm-connect

This page is for anyone, a person or an agent, working on an
application that uses elm-connect: changing its protos, regenerating
its Elm client, or fixing a build. [README.md](README.md) maps the rest
of the documentation. To change elm-connect itself, read
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) instead. `elm-connect guide` prints this
page, so a reader with only the binary has it too.

## Generated files are output

Every module elm-connect writes starts with a line such as
`-- Generated by elm-connect 0.2.0 from notes/v1/notes.proto`. Never
edit one: the next run overwrites it, and `check` reports the edit as
drift. To change what a generated module says, change the proto or the
generator's options ([generator.md](generator.md#options)) and
regenerate.

Regenerate after every proto change, with the same files, include
paths and options as before; the project's build script, Makefile or
`buf.gen.yaml` usually records them. `gen` deletes nothing: a module the
protos no longer give stays on disk, and `gen` names it in a warning.

## Check before and after

`elm-connect check` takes exactly `gen`'s arguments and writes nothing.
It exits 0 when the generated modules are current, 1 when one is
missing, differs (with a diff) or is stale, and 2 when it cannot tell
([generator.md](generator.md#checking-generated-code-elm-connect-check)).

- Before a change, run it to learn whether the tree was current. If it
  was not, someone edited a generated file or forgot to regenerate;
  say so before mixing that drift into your change.
- After the change, regenerate, then run it again: 0 means the
  committed modules are what the protos give. The diff of the generated
  modules is what the change does to the Elm code that uses them.

With protoc or buf, which have no `check`, regenerate and run `git diff
--exit-code` over the output directory.

## Reading a diagnostic

A problem fails the run and prints a code, such as
`naming::type_collision`, above its message, with the proto line it is
about. [diagnostics.md](diagnostics.md) lists every code and its escape:
the option or the proto edit that gets past it. The help text under the
message names the fix for this case. Prefer the escape the table gives;
do not work around a diagnostic by editing generated code.

A collision or a reserved name (`naming::*_collision`,
`naming::reserved_name`, `naming::reserved_module`) means two proto
names become one Elm name, or a generated name takes one Elm or the
runtime already uses. Both ways out change names the application's
code uses, so choose deliberately; an agent should put the choice to
the user:

- `--rename <proto full name>:<Elm name>` (`rename=` for the plugin)
  renames one element in the generated code, leaving the proto alone;
- `--module-prefix Api` (`module_prefix=Api`) moves every generated
  module under a prefix, which settles a module name clash with the
  runtime or a package;
- or rename the element in the proto, which changes it for every client.

`naming::runtime_namespace` and `naming::shadowing_module` are
warnings: the run succeeds, but a generated module may clash later or
cannot be imported beside a package. The same two options settle them.

## The application's `elm.json`

Generated code imports the runtime's `Proto.*` and `Rpc.*` modules.
[install.md](install.md#the-runtime) has a complete `elm.json` for an
application outside this repository, and the packages that must be
direct dependencies. A `MODULE NOT FOUND` naming `Bytes`, `Http`, `Json`
or `Time` from a runtime module means one of them is missing.
A compile error at `elmConnectVersion_` means the generated code and
the runtime come from different releases: regenerate with the matching
generator, or use the runtime the generated code names
([install.md](install.md#versions)).

## Seeing a request without a server

`Rpc.request` gives the HTTP request a call stands for, without sending
it, so `elm repl` in the application's directory shows the method, URL,
headers and body of any call under either protocol
([quickstart.md](quickstart.md#6-try-it-in-elm-repl)). `Rpc.response`
reads a canned answer, so a test can check a call end to end without a
server ([quickstart.md](quickstart.md#7-test-without-a-server)).

## Not built yet

Machine-readable diagnostics and `elm-connect --explain <code>` are on
the roadmap
([Agent affordances in the CLI](roadmap.md#agent-affordances-in-the-cli));
until then, read the rendered output and the catalogue.
